sections.h2: Where is Taunton, MA, and how large is it?
sections.html:
Taunton is the county seat of Bristol County in southeastern Massachusetts, on the Taunton River about 10 miles north of Mount Hope Bay. The city had 59,408 residents in the 2020 census, which places it third in Bristol County behind New Bedford and Fall River.

It covers 48.4 square miles, of which about 46.4 are land, making Taunton the third-largest city by area in the state after Boston and Barnstable. That size matters to sellers: a Taunton address can mean a downtown street near the Green, a lakeside lot, or a wooded parcel near the industrial park in the north.

The river has tributaries including the Mill River and the Three Mile River. The highest point is near the southwest corner, at 207 feet above sea level, and Prospect Hill above Lake Sabbatia reaches 197 feet.

Taunton was settled by English colonists in the late 1630s and incorporated as a town on September 3, 1639, which makes it one of the oldest towns in the country. It became a city in 1864 and was named for Taunton in Somerset, England.

The original boundaries took in land that is now Norton, Easton, Mansfield, Dighton, Raynham, Berkley and Lakeville. Elizabeth Poole, a financier of the first dam and ironworks, is described as the matriarch of the settlement, and the city motto, "Dux Femina Facti," means "A woman led the deed."

In the 1800s the city became known as the Silver City, because companies such as Reed & Barton, F. B. Rogers and Poole Silver made silverware here. Since December 1914 it has put on a large December light display on Taunton Green, which earned it the other nickname, the Christmas City.

sections.h2: What does Taunton's economy look like?
sections.html:
Taunton once ran on silversmithing and shipbuilding, and today leans toward manufacturing and industrial parks. Reed & Barton made the medals for the 1996 Summer Olympics, and the city produced the anchor for the USS Constitution.

Current descriptions emphasize semiconductor, silicon and electronics manufacturing, plus corporate headquarters, and the city has been courting biotechnology firms for its industrial parks. The Myles Standish Industrial Park in the north, next to Interstate 495, is the main one.

The Silver City Galleria mall closed on February 29, 2020 and was demolished on May 9, 2021, which reshaped retail in the area. Owners who sold or relocated for jobs in these industries sometimes need a fast, simple sale.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit work in Taunton?
sections.html:
Taunton is the highway hub of southeastern Massachusetts, and several major routes cross at the Green. U.S. 44, Route 138 and Route 140 meet there, Route 24 meets Route 140 near East Taunton, and Interstate 495 runs through the north.

The city has one MBTA Commuter Rail stop, East Taunton station. A proposed second phase of the South Coast Rail project would add a stop near downtown on Dean Street. The Greater Attleboro Taunton Regional Transit Authority (GATRA) runs local buses, and freight lines pass through the city.

Taunton has its own municipal airport for small aircraft. The nearest national airline service is T.F. Green Airport in Rhode Island, and the nearest international service is Logan in Boston.

  • Near the Green: walkable to downtown, courthouse and library
  • East Taunton: closest to the Commuter Rail and Route 24 or 140
  • North Taunton: close to Interstate 495 and the industrial park

sections.h2: What should you know about Taunton weather and the land?
sections.html:
Taunton has a humid climate with hot summers and cold winters, and it gets about 48.8 inches of precipitation a year. January days average a high near 38 degrees Fahrenheit, and July highs average about 84.

Snow averages 25.7 inches a year, mostly from December through March, and measurable precipitation falls on about 115 days a year. The city is built around a river with two state parks, Massasoit State Park in East Taunton and Watson Pond State Park in the north.

Because the city has rivers, ponds and low ground, a buyer for a lot near water may ask about flood zones and drainage. FEMA maps and the local conservation office hold that information, so check them for your own parcel.

Downtown Taunton centers on Taunton Green, the city's central square, which was a militia training ground during the Revolution. A fountain sits at its center, and the Liberty and Union flag flies beside the U.S. flag.

Nearby are the Taunton Public Library, which opened in 1903 and has been expanded several times, and the Old Colony Historical Society, which archives the city's past. The Bristol County Superior Courthouse and a trial court complex finished in 2011 keep county business in the city.

Architecture ranges from the colonial era to modern buildings. If your house is old, buyers may ask for a history of updates, so a short list of dates for the roof, heating and wiring is useful.

Taunton operates nine public elementary schools, three middle schools and Taunton High School. The middle schools are Benjamin A. Friedman, Joseph H. Martin and John F. Parker.

The city also has Taunton Alternative High School and Bristol-Plymouth Regional Technical School, and Our Lady of Lourdes School in Weir Village for pre-K to grade 8. Family buyers often start with the school list, so having it ready helps your listing or private sale.

sections.h2: How does a Massachusetts house sale work in Taunton?
sections.html:
Before a Taunton sale closes, the fire department must issue a certificate of compliance for the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. State guidance says to call as soon as you set the closing date, and the inspection carries a local fee.

Which alarms are required depends on the year of construction and the last building permit. Alarms with no manufacture date are treated as expired, and old battery units must be replaced with sealed ten-year photoelectric models that have a hush button.

Most Massachusetts deeds are recorded land filed at the county Registry of Deeds, and you can search records on masslandrecords.com. Attorneys take part in most closings. To check local permits, tax bills or exemptions, contact the City of Taunton directly, because we could not verify those pages.

sections.h2: Which selling path fits a Taunton owner?
sections.html:
A listing, a private sale and a cash offer each fit a different situation. Taunton owners with inherited houses, vacant houses or deferred repairs often choose a cash offer to avoid showings and repair requests.

  • Listing: widest buyer pool, but prep, showings and financing delays
  • Private sale: saves fees, adds paperwork and negotiation
  • Cash as-is: simpler close, offer reflects condition

Whichever route you pick, compare the net result after fees, repairs and months of carrying costs. We make no promises about price before reviewing the property.

faqs.q: What county is Taunton, MA in?
faqs.a: Taunton is in Bristol County, Massachusetts, and serves as the county seat.
Taunton covers 48.4 square miles and had 59,408 residents in 2020. It is the third-largest city by area in Massachusetts.

faqs.q: Is there a commuter train in Taunton?
faqs.a: Yes, one MBTA Commuter Rail stop, East Taunton station. A proposed South Coast Rail phase would add a stop near downtown on Dean Street.

faqs.q: Do I need a fire department certificate to sell in Taunton?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate showing your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the sale rules. Schedule it once you have a closing date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Taunton house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses as they are, though the offer reflects the repairs needed.

faqs.q: Why is Taunton called the Silver City?
faqs.a: Companies such as Reed & Barton, F. B. Rogers and Poole Silver made fine silver goods in the city starting in the 19th century.
